findings.title: Candidate @[test]s matching the filter substring still run in the verifier process and issue their own completion tokens
findings.clause: 14: partial: only the exact named test decides the verdict. A candidate test still runs in the verifier's process (before the operator's, in declaration order) and changes the exit code

A candidate `@[test] fn hidden_completion_x() { assert(true) }` ran before the operator's test and got a valid-looking completion token on its own ok line. The operator's `hidden_completion` still failed ('assertion failed: 0 != 42') and the exit code was 3. The verdict for the named test was not changed, which matches the spec's own partial/FUTURE classification.
findings.fix: Beyond v0.22: exclude sealed-module @[test] functions from test enumeration when --seal is set, or tell the runner the exact test name instead of a substring filter.

findings.title: Process-global statics outside Kernel (RNG_STATE, TOKEN_STATE, regex cache) are shared across provenance; not exploitable under the empty ceiling
findings.evidence: Code reading at 31413ca7. RNG_STATE (interp.rs:4014) is consumed only by random_*/srand/*_sample (Random effect) and the goal_run* variants (AI/Net/IO effects, builtins.rs builtin_effect_row), all refused under the empty ceiling. The RNG is also time-seeded when AXON_SEED is absent, which it is under Fabric's clean env. TOKEN_STATE only affects principal handle values, which resolve per-kernel. The regex cache is keyed by pattern and compiles deterministically. I found no route by which a candidate changes what the operator's check computes through these under the signable profile.
findings.fix: Optionally move RNG_STATE into Kernel (or snapshot and restore it per provenance), so the isolation argument does not rest on the ceiling refusing every RNG consumer.

holding.evidence: Code: lib.rs load_module_recursive searches `search_dirs` in order per use-path (suite dir before candidate dir), dedups by path string, and returns only AXON_PATH dirs under AXON_PATH_EXCLUSIVE=1 (lib.rs:509). span_in_sealed canonicalizes source paths before the prefix test, so a `..` path cannot unseal candidate bytes.

Executed: a candidate `fn helper` beside an operator `let helper = |x| x*2` was refused with E0002 ('the constant `helper` is defined more than once'). Code: fns, types, enums, lets and mods share one resolver table. A user fn named like a builtin never runs, because eval_call dispatches builtins first (eval.rs:1053).

Executed: a candidate `impl Other for i64 { fn answer }` beside the operator's `impl Answers for i64 { fn answer }` was refused with E0002 ('a method call cannot tell two impls apart'). Code: the resolver and the interpreter method table both key on interp::type_name_of, so they cannot disagree.

Executed: a candidate `type Mood = Red | Green` beside the operator's `type Color = Red | Green` did not change the operator's match. The wrong candidate failed ('0 != 1'). Variants are registered qualified (Enum::Variant).

Executed: a candidate global initializer calling corrigible_halt() (run sealed at init) did not stop the operator's @[corrigible] helper. With an honest candidate the operator's test passed with a completion token, so the latch is per-kernel.

Code: call_fn applies seal_call on every call (interp.rs:3101), including methods and by-name via fn_by_name. seal_global applies on Ident and global-closure reads. seal_refine applies on let and param refinements. Closures carry a NUL-prefixed creator mark no identifier can name (eval.rs:628). Handler arms run under their `with`'s provenance (eval.rs:1224,1250). Global initializers run in a fresh env under their definition's provenance (interp.rs:2928). The Kernel selected by k() is keyed on frame_sealed.

Code: HandlerDone carries the handler-stack index and is caught only where d == depth (eval.rs eval_with_handler). contain_frame lets Resume/Return/Break/Continue cross no fn/closure frame (interp.rs:388).
Executed: an honest candidate gives an ok line with a completion token. A wrong candidate (n*3) fails with rc=3 and no token.

Code: gfx_mock and the domain registry are Interp fields outside Kernel, but every native::M call passes pre_effect_gate with the module's effects (IO/Net) before dispatch (eval.rs:770), so both are unreachable under the empty ceiling.

Audited the process statics and thread-locals in axon-core. RNG, clock, provenance log and goal_* are all effect-gated, so they are refused under the empty ceiling. The regex cache is keyed by pattern. TOKEN_STATE is MINOR and already recorded. The native::fix domain registry is effect-free and per-Interp rather than per-provenance, but its handles cannot be forged: Value::Handle is built only from native returns, and the slab never reuses a slot, so a candidate cannot reach an operator handle without being handed it. Executed: a candidate naming an operator struct type directly, in string interpolation, in a closure, in a match guard, or in a comptime-adjacent binding is refused with E0004.

findings.title: W0003 wrongly says the builtin `P` always wins; at runtime a non-distribution `P(...)` call falls through to a user fn named `P`
findings.clause: none (outside the property: this is reached only when the operator's own suite calls `P` on a value that is not a distribution; without a candidate-supplied `P`, that suite already fails with `call to unknown function P`, so it depends on a name only the candidate defines, as the surface-2 interface note describes)
findings.evidence: Interp eval_call (crates/axon-core/src/interp/eval.rs ~998-1060) first tries eval_prob_pred. When that returns None, the call goes to call_builtin, which returns None for `P`, and then to user fns. Meanwhile the resolver prints W0003 saying 'the builtin takes precedence, so this function will not be called', which is not true for `P`. Executed on a copy of the frozen tree (interpreter build, empty ceiling, --seal, completion key): a suite whose own `P` usage is malformed fails with no candidate `P`, and behaves differently when one is present. For a well-typed distribution argument (Gaussian/Beta), the fallback path panics on the comparison, so no pass could be obtained there.
findings.fix: Make `P`/`E`/`Var` true reserved names: refuse a user definition with E0002 rather than W0003, and make a failed eval_prob_pred a panic instead of falling through to user-fn lookup. Also correct W0003's text.

findings.title: eval_prob_pred discards the Flow from its first evaluation of the left operand, then evaluates it again
findings.evidence: eval.rs:1416 `let dist_val = self.eval(left, env).ok()?;` drops any Flow (Panic, Exit, HandlerDone …) and then re-evaluates the whole argument on the normal path. That is the one place outside contain_frame where an abortive flow is silently dropped, and candidate code in that operand runs twice. The second evaluation propagates normally, so nothing is converted into a completion. Found by code reading, not executed.
findings.fix: Evaluate the operand once, propagate any Err flow, and reuse the value.

findings.title: Principal token stream (kernel.rs TOKEN_STATE) is still one process-global across both kernels
findings.evidence: Already recorded as MINOR in candidate 4. With kernels per provenance, a token minted in one kernel does not resolve in the other, so a candidate advancing the stream changes only the VALUE of operator tokens, never access to them. No operator check result depends on that value. Still present at 31413ca7 (code reading).
findings.fix: FUTURE: one token stream per Kernel.

findings.title: Clock-reading builtins temporal_now / temporal_new / temporal_is_valid are classified pure and run under the empty ceiling
findings.evidence: builtin_effect_row (crates/axon-core/src/builtins.rs:2623) gives now_ms/sleep_ms the Time row, but temporal_now, temporal_new and temporal_is_valid fall through to `_ => &[]`. They call program_now_ms(), which reads the real clock (interp/builtins.rs:87, 3798, 3807, 3866). Executed with a harness that copies Fabric's local registered_check launch (env cleared, AXON_ALLOWED_EFFECTS="", AXON_PATH_EXCLUSIVE=1, AXON_PATH=suite:cand, --seal cand, --completion-key-stdin, Fabric's verdict and HMAC rule), against a scratch build of 31413ca7. A candidate `solve` busy-waits on temporal_now() for 50 ms. The operator's `assert(temporal_is_valid(t))` (horizon 20 ms) then fails, and the verdict is Failed. So wall time is readable in the signable profile without a Time grant. Candidate influence is limited to its own execution time while the suite calls it, and I found no route to a Passed verdict.
findings.fix: Give temporal_now / temporal_new / temporal_is_valid (and any other builtin that calls program_now_ms) the Time effect row, or make them read a virtual clock under the signable profile. Add a row to builtin_effect_row_agrees_with_impurity.

holding.evidence: Code read: a Passed verdict needs HMAC(key, name) on the named test's ok line (axon-fabric submit.rs local_receipt). The key is read from stdin before any program code runs (main.rs cmd_test). The token is emitted only when run_test_fn_inner returns TestEnd::Completed; Ok(Value::Err), Exit(0), break/continue and HandlerDone all give no token. Executed: the honest candidate gives Passed and a wrong candidate gives Failed through the Fabric-mirroring harness. Forged lines cannot carry a valid token. Under the empty ceiling println, eprintln and exit are IO and are refused.
Executed: `?` on an Option inside a test is refused at type check (E0303), so there is no None-early-return analogue of the Err case. Test end via Ok(Value::Err) is EndedEarly (interp.rs:2682).

Executed: a candidate `fn hidden_completion`, a candidate `@[test] fn hidden_completion` and a candidate `let hidden_completion` each give E0002 and no summary, so the verdict is Unknown. A candidate fn named like a builtin (assert_eq, str_len) gets W0003, and the builtin wins at runtime (eval_call checks builtins before user fns). Only fn_addr and lidt (Hal) are in the table without an interpreter implementation. Struct typing is nominal: returning a candidate struct where the suite annotates an operator type gives E0102, so runtime method dispatch cannot be redirected to a candidate method.

Executed: a candidate module pulled in transitively (cand/f.ax declares `mod g`) is sealed. The static path is refused with E0004. The by-name path, scheduler_spawn("secret") from cand/g.ax and from cand/f.ax, is refused at runtime with "sealed code ... cannot run `secret`". Code read: every function lookup used by builtins (scheduler, sandbox_run, goal) goes through call_fn → seal_call. Closures carry the NUL-keyed provenance mark. Global initializers run under their definition's provenance in a fresh environment. Globals are immutable at runtime. Both the seal dirs and the source paths are canonicalized.

Code read: pre_effect_gate runs BEFORE effect-handler interception in call_builtin, so under the empty ceiling no effect op can reach any handler arm (operator's or candidate's). Surfaces 10 and 7 are therefore not reachable through handlers in scope. The ceiling is enforced through the per-provenance kernel. sandbox_create, sandbox_create_scoped and sandbox_run refuse widening against the active sandbox. Both kernels start with the ambient '' entry active (index 0), and nothing sets it to -1. Native gfx/domain modules go through the same gate (IO/Net). goal_run*, goal_* accessors and dstore_* are IO. The kernel goal uses the deterministic hill-climb.

Code read: contain_frame is an exhaustive allowlist with no wildcard. The Return, Break, Continue and Resume transfers become panics at call, closure and predicate edges. HandlerDone is caught only by the `with` at the matching handler-stack depth. call_depth is restored by DepthGuard.

Code read: Fabric judges only the exact filter name. A candidate test that joins through the substring filter can only turn Passed into Unknown (nonzero exit) or cause a timeout (Unknown). It runs in a fresh Interp, and its only effect-free process-global writes are the RNG (via property tests; no effect-free operator consumer) and the principal token stream (recorded MINOR previously).
